summary: A 1979 list of assigned numbers used in network protocols. It replaced RFC 750 and was replaced by RFC 758. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 755 updates a collection of number assignments used by network protocols, including an expanded list of network numbers and internet protocol numbers. It was later replaced by RFC 758.

questions: what is udp's assigned protocol number
subtitle: An updated registry of numbers assigned to network protocols in 1979

tldr.problem: Number assignments for network protocols changed, so the shared registry needed another update.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists current link, socket, network, internet message version, protocol number, format and message type assignments.
tldr.outcome: RFC 755 was historic and was later replaced by RFC 758.

today: RFC 755 is Historic and has been obsoleted by RFC 758.

sections.title: Purpose of the Registry
sections.content:
RFC 755 documents values assigned in several series used by network protocol implementations. It says the registry will be updated periodically and identifies Jon Postel as the person handling assignments and maintaining current information.

Developers whose protocol or application needs a link, socket or similar number are asked to request an assignment. The RFC points to the Protocol Handbook and other documents for protocol details.
sections.plainLanguage: This is an updated collection of number assignments used by network protocols. Developers were told to request a number when a new protocol needed one.

sections.title: Updated Number Lists
sections.content:
The RFC lists link numbers, socket numbers, network numbers, internet message versions, internet protocol numbers and internet message types. It also describes an 8-bit internet protocol number field and a 4-bit message-version field.

The network-number table assigns values to networks and leaves other values unassigned or reserved. The internet protocol number table includes UDP at 17 and lists other protocol values alongside their meanings or references.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry has separate tables for different number fields. The tables show assigned values, including UDP's entry, and mark values that remain unassigned or reserved.

sections.title: Registry History and Status
sections.content:
RFC 755 identifies RFC 750, 739, 604, 503, 433 and 349 as obsoleted by this edition. The assigned-number lists are intended to be updated periodically as protocol assignments change.

The unit metadata records RFC 758 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 755.
sections.plainLanguage: This edition replaced several earlier assignment lists and was itself replaced later. The sequence reflects that the registry was updated over time.
